angle: The first ROI from AI often comes between steps, not inside them—redesign handoffs before models.
sourceTitle: Cutting the ‘coordination tax’: How agentic AI can reshape workflows
linkedinPost:
Most AI value is hiding in the handoffs.

McKinsey’s new piece on agentic AI nails a lesson we see every week: the biggest productivity drag isn’t the work itself, it’s the “coordination tax” between teams and systems.

Think of the places where tickets stall, approvals ping-pong, or data gets copy-pasted across tools. That’s where agent-style automation can quietly pay for itself.

My take from the FDE trenches: don’t start by “AI-ifying” an entire process. Start by surgically removing two or three high-friction handoffs. Examples we’ve shipped: bots that prep cross-team intake packets, agents that reconcile IDs between CRM and billing, and auto-drafters that assemble 80% of a handoff brief for humans to finalize.

Three rules that separate winners from pilot purgatory:
- Design the future handoff first; pick the model second.
- Give the agent a narrow, well-instrumented scope with clear SLAs.
- Measure cycle time and rework, not just “tasks automated.”

If you can cut one handoff from 3 days to 3 hours, scaling becomes a budgeting exercise, not a science project.

Where is your worst handoff—and what would a 10x faster version unlock? #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI #AIAdoption
